title: dinky configuration
description: ~/.config/dinky/dinky.toml. Every key is optional; a key left out keeps its default.

start-at-login.description: Register dinky as a login item.

workspaces.description: Workspaces across all displays, numbered from 1, one native Space each. dinky creates and removes Spaces to match.

workspace-to-display.description: By workspace number, the display it lives on: a pattern (main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name as `dinky list-displays` prints it) or a list of them, the first that matches a connected display winning. Other workspaces, and these when no pattern matches, live on the main display.

default-layout.description: Workspace layout. tiles is the original name for dwindle; free tiles nothing, every window floats.

default-tiling.description: Whether dinky tiles numbered workspaces by default.

workspace.description: Tiling overrides for numbered workspaces on every display (1-based).

layout.description: free floats every window on the workspace, whatever tiling says, and tiles it again on a workspace with another layout.

columns.description: Reserved columns for a fixed layout.

rows.description: Reserved rows for a fixed layout.

expand.description: Where overflow windows go when every fixed cell is full.

follow-app-activation.description: When Cmd-Tab or a Dock click activates an app on another Space, switch there with the fast switch.

float-windows-without-fullscreen.description: Float windows that can't go full screen, such as Finder's copy progress, About This Mac and Calculator. A `layout tiling` rule tiles one anyway.

menu-bar-icon.description: blocks shows a block per display with the workspace it shows, the focused display's filled. text shows the focused display's workspace number. none hides it.

hide-menu-bar-icon.description: When to hide dinky's menu bar item. single-display hides it while only one display is connected. always hides it, as menu-bar-icon = 'none' does. never leaves it to menu-bar-icon.

scripting-addition.description: Whether dinky may use its Dock scripting addition (SIP off). Where it is injected, a scrolling strip scrolls through it; without it, or false, the strip moves its windows frame by frame. false never checks for or injects it, even with SIP off.

highlight-color.description: What every highlight left unset takes: the switchers' pick, the focused window's border, the noop glow and a drag's preview. Unset, each keeps its own default.

haptic.description: Whether the trackpad taps for dinky: what every haptic left unset takes, the strip's ticks ([gestures.scroll]), a bound swipe's tap ([gestures.trackpad]) and the switchers' picks ([switcher]).

haptic-strength.description: How strongly: what every haptic-strength left unset takes.

column-width.description: A new column's width as a share of the display. A lone column fills the display.

center-focused-column.description: Where focusing a column scrolls it, as niri's center-focused-column: never just far enough to show it whole, always to the middle of the display, end columns too, always-fill to the middle but never past the strip's ends, so end columns go only to the display's edge and it stays filled, on-overflow to the middle only when it did not all show. Columns that all fit stay centred as a whole.

span-center-on.description: With span-displays, which display center-focused-column centres a column on: both centres on the two together, so the column rests beside the line between them; mouse on the display under the pointer; focused on the display the column is on as focus comes to it. Focus stepping along the strip never scrolls it back.

span-height.description: With span-displays, how tall the strip's columns are on displays of different heights: per-display as the display a column's middle is on, changing once as that crosses between them, on the way to a shorter display a little before; overlap as high as both displays have room, top edges lined up, so nothing changes size crossing; at-rest as the display a column rests on, keeping its size while fingers or the mouse hold the strip and changing once they let go.

span-width.description: With span-displays, what column-width is a share of while a strip runs across both displays: display, one display, as on one display, so 0.5 is half a display; merged, both together as one wide display, so 0.5 is a display. A column is never wider than a display.

span-height-animate.description: With span-displays and span-height = 'per-display', ease a window's height between the displays' as it crosses: down to the shorter display's as it comes to it, finished just before it shows there, and up to the taller's along the glide, rather than stepping. Each step resizes the window, which slow apps follow less closely.

span-peek.description: With span-displays, whether columns scrolled off the outer edges of the two displays peek out there, as on one display. false keeps no gutter for them: they tuck under the column in view with 2 points on, keeping their sizes, and the columns fill out to the outer gaps.

span-displays.description: Prototype: with exactly two displays side by side, each showing a scrolling workspace, run one strip across both. Switching one display to a Space switches the other to the Space at the same place among its own, the companion dinky makes there for each workspace, whatever its layout.

fullscreen.description: dinky's fullscreen, a window filling its workspace over the tree.

focus-change.description: What focusing another window of the workspace does while one is fullscreen: exit ends fullscreen, follow makes the newly focused window fullscreen in its place, keep makes it fullscreen too.

follow-delay-ms.description: With focus-change = 'follow', how long the newly focused window waits before going fullscreen, so the other window is back in its tile first. 0 swaps them at once.

scrolling.description: On a scrolling workspace: push widens the window's column to the screen and slides its neighbours off, over covers the columns where they are.

floating.description: What tiling commands do to a floating window.

move-step.description: Points `move` shifts a floating window by, unless the binding gives a number.

resize-anchor.description: What stays put when `resize` sizes a floating window: its centre, or its top-left corner so it grows right and down.

padding.description: Points by which neighbouring windows peek out.

orientation.description: What a container's orientation becomes when it switches to accordion: auto runs along its longer side, keep keeps the orientation it had.

display.description: Overrides for one display, keyed by pattern: main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name as `dinky list-displays` prints it.

active-color.description: Colour of the focused window's border. Unset, the top-level highlight-color, or #e1e3e4 without one.

order.description: below draws the border directly below the window. above draws it above, as a ring that never covers the window's content or takes clicks.

exclude-apps.description: Bundle IDs whose windows get no border.

noop-flash.description: Make the focused window's edge glow once when a key binding or gesture does nothing. Drawn even when borders are off.

noop-flash-color.description: Colour of the ring around the window and of the glow inside it. Unset, the top-level highlight-color, or #d97757 (Claude's orange) without one.

noop-flash-width.description: The ring around the window, in points; 0 leaves it out.

noop-flash-spread.description: How far the glow inside the window reaches in, fading as it goes, in points.

noop-flash-opacity.description: The glow's opacity at the window's edge, as a share of the colour's own; 0 leaves it out.

pinned.description: Ring the windows of a pinned column in pinned-color, focused or not. Drawn even when borders are off.

pinned-color.description: Colour of the pinned windows' ring. Unset, the top-level highlight-color, or #d97757 (Claude's orange) without one.

pinned-width.description: The pinned windows' ring, in points; 0 leaves it out.

focus-follows-mouse.description: Focus the window under the pointer once the pointer rests on it.

delay-ms.description: How long the pointer must rest on a window before it takes focus. 0 focuses as soon as the pointer stops.

accordion-edges.description: Whether resting on the peeking edge of an accordion child focuses it.

animations.description: Windows glide to their tiles instead of jumping. Off while macOS's Reduce Motion is on.

duration-ms.description: Roughly how long a window takes to arrive on the spring, exactly how long along an easing. 0 jumps. 363 with damping 1 is SlideScroll's spring.

damping.description: How the spring settles: 1 eases into place without overshooting; lower gets there sooner and overshoots, more the lower.

curve.description: How windows travel: on a spring, or along an easings.net timing function over duration-ms.

drag.description: Dragging a tiled window with the mouse.

placeholders.description: While you drag a tiled window, outline the tile it came from, and show over the tile under the pointer the part the window will take.

preview-border-color.description: Border of the part of the tile a dragged window will take. Unset, the top-level highlight-color, or the system accent colour without one.

preview-fill-color.description: Fill of that part. Unset, the border colour at 30%.

home-outline.description: Outline the tile a dragged window came from. false shows only the feedback over the tile under the pointer.

preview-border-width.description: Points, for every border while you drag: the preview, a swap's, and the outlines of the tiles.

mouse-modifier.description: Held exactly, drag a window from anywhere in it, not only by its title bar: alt, ctrl, cmd or shift, or several joined by -, such as ctrl-cmd. Once set, only a drag with it held drops onto a tile; a tiled window dragged by its title bar alone goes back. The press goes to dinky, not the app. The key's side follows [modifiers]; none turns it off.

switcher.description: What [window-switcher] and [workspace-switcher] share. Each key can go in either of them too, for that switcher alone.

enabled.description: Whether the switchers show at all: false turns off the modifier, the bindings and the swipes.

delay-ms.description: How long the modifier is held alone before the capsule shows.

trigger.description: How the modifier shows the capsule. hold: held alone for delay-ms, released to take the pick. double-tap: tapped alone twice; the capsule stays up for the keys, the pointer or a click, as from a key binding.

double-tap-ms.description: With double-tap, how long each tap and the gap between them may last.

corner-radius.description: The capsule's corner radius in points. Half its height or more makes round ends.

position.description: Where the capsule shows on the display under the pointer. auto: over the pointer when held or swiped, in the middle from a key binding. center: the middle. top: below the menu bar. bottom: above the Dock. mouse: over the pointer, from a key binding too.

show-titles.description: Whether windows show their titles: under each card in the window switcher (on a map, and over a column's upper window, on a band along its foot), on a band along each window's foot in a workspace card (not a covered or tiny window's, nor with schematic thumbnails). A window without a title shows its app's name.

letter-keys.description: Whether each window gets a letter, drawn as a key at its title's right; pressing it while the capsule is up jumps to the window: the window switcher focuses it, the workspace switcher switches to its workspace and focuses it.

letters.description: The letters handed out, in order, to the windows as they read, left to right. Lowercase a to z, each once, without h, j, k and l, which move the pick.

highlight-color.description: The pick's ring and the glow under it. Unset, the top-level highlight-color, or the system accent colour without one.

haptic.description: Whether the trackpad taps as the pick moves. Unset, the top-level haptic.

haptic-strength.description: How strongly. Unset, the top-level haptic-strength.

window-switcher.description: Hold the modifier alone over a workspace for a capsule of its windows at the pointer; release to focus the one picked.

enabled.description: Whether this switcher shows at all; [switcher]'s when left out.

modifier.description: The modifier that shows the capsule; none turns it off. The key's side follows [modifiers].

delay-ms.description: How long the modifier is held alone before the capsule shows; [switcher]'s when left out.

trigger.description: How the modifier shows the capsule, as [switcher]'s trigger; [switcher]'s when left out.

double-tap-ms.description: With double-tap, how long each tap and the gap between them may last; [switcher]'s when left out.

layouts.description: The layouts the capsule shows for. tiles is dwindle; free is a workspace dinky does not tile, its windows in a row left to right.

corner-radius.description: The capsule's corner radius in points; [switcher]'s when left out.

tiles-style.description: How a tiles or fixed workspace shows: map, its tiles where they are, picked in two dimensions, or row, like a scrolling workspace.

show-single.description: Whether the capsule shows for a workspace with a lone tiled window (on a free workspace, a lone window), held or from a binding. false shows it only with two or more.

show-titles.description: Whether each window's title shows under its card, as [switcher]'s show-titles; [switcher]'s when left out.

position.description: Where the capsule shows, as [switcher]'s position; [switcher]'s when left out.

letter-keys.description: As [switcher]'s letter-keys, for this switcher alone; [switcher]'s when left out.

letters.description: As [switcher]'s letters, for this switcher alone; [switcher]'s when left out.

highlight-color.description: The pick's ring and the glow under it; [switcher]'s when left out.

haptic.description: Whether the trackpad taps as the pick moves; [switcher]'s when left out.

workspace-switcher.description: Hold the modifier alone for a capsule of the workspaces at the pointer, each drawn small in its layout; release to switch to the one picked.

enabled.description: Whether this switcher shows at all; [switcher]'s when left out.

modifier.description: The modifier that shows the capsule; none turns it off. Not the same as [window-switcher]'s unless their triggers differ. The key's side follows [modifiers].

delay-ms.description: How long the modifier is held alone before the capsule shows; [switcher]'s when left out.

trigger.description: How the modifier shows the capsule, as [switcher]'s trigger; [switcher]'s when left out.

double-tap-ms.description: With double-tap, how long each tap and the gap between them may last; [switcher]'s when left out.

displays.description: all: every display's workspaces, a group per display. pointer: only the display under the pointer.

show-fullscreen.description: A card for each native full-screen Space, after its display's workspaces.

card-height.description: Each card's height in points; its width follows its display's proportions.

thumbnails.description: windows: a picture of each window, needing Screen Recording. icons: each window's app icon. schematic: a fixed picture of each workspace's layout, the same whatever its windows.

corner-radius.description: The capsule's corner radius in points; [switcher]'s when left out.

position.description: Where the capsule shows, as [switcher]'s position; [switcher]'s when left out.

show-titles.description: Whether each window in a card shows its title on a band along its foot, as [switcher]'s show-titles; [switcher]'s when left out.

letter-keys.description: As [switcher]'s letter-keys, for this switcher alone; [switcher]'s when left out.

letters.description: As [switcher]'s letters, for this switcher alone; [switcher]'s when left out.

highlight-color.description: The pick's ring, the glow under it and, with schematic thumbnails, the picked card's windows; [switcher]'s when left out.

haptic.description: Whether the trackpad taps as the pick moves; [switcher]'s when left out.

hud.description: A glass capsule naming the new layout or binding mode for a moment after it changes.

position.description: bottom: above the Dock, or near the bottom of the screen when the Dock hides or sits at a side. top: below the menu bar.

duration-ms.description: How long it stays before fading out. Another change meanwhile restarts the count.

offset.description: Points between the capsule and the Dock or menu bar.

on-layout-change.description: Show it after the layout command.

on-mode-change.description: Show it when the binding mode changes.

on-workspace-change.description: Show the workspace's number and layout when a display moves to another workspace.

on-noop.description: Show why when a key binding or gesture does nothing.

gestures.description: Swipes on the trackpad and on a Magic Mouse, each running a command or commands as a key binding does, and fingers on the trackpad scrolling a strip. A swipe that shows a switcher goes on picking with the same fingers until they lift.

trackpad.description: Swipes on the trackpad with `fingers` fingers.

enabled.description: false turns swipes on the trackpad off.

fingers.description: How many fingers swipe. 2 also scrolls.

distance.description: Millimetres the fingers move, mostly one way, before it is a swipe.

step.description: Millimetres the fingers move for each step of a switcher's pick.

haptic.description: Whether the trackpad taps as a bound swipe runs. Unset, the top-level haptic.

haptic-strength.description: How strongly. Unset, the top-level haptic-strength.

mouse.description: The same swipes on a Magic Mouse. Its own swipes replace all of the trackpad's; without any, those run.

enabled.description: true swipes on the mouse too.

fingers.description: How many fingers swipe on the mouse. Two also swipe between full-screen apps unless that is off.

distance.description: Millimetres the fingers move, mostly one way, before it is a swipe.

step.description: Millimetres the fingers move for each step of a switcher's pick.

scroll.description: Fingers moved across the trackpad scroll the strip under the pointer with them, after SlideScroll; let go, it coasts on and settles with the column nearest the middle in view.

enabled.description: true scrolls strips with the fingers.

fingers.description: How many fingers scroll. Not [gestures.trackpad]'s fingers while it binds swipe-left or swipe-right.

speed.description: How many screens the strip moves as the fingers cross the whole trackpad.

show-switcher.description: Whether the window switcher shows the strip once it rests after the fingers let go, the window taking focus picked.

switcher-ms.description: Milliseconds the window switcher shows the strip with show-switcher.

edge-flash.description: Whether the display glows along its left or right side as the fingers push the strip on past that end, in the noop flash's look.

haptic.description: Whether the trackpad ticks each time the column a let-go would settle on changes under the fingers. Unset, the top-level haptic.

haptic-strength.description: How strongly. Unset, the top-level haptic-strength.

mouse-scroll.description: With the modifier held, the mouse scrolls the strip under the pointer as fingers on the trackpad do: a press dragged across, or a swipe or wheel stroke; a wheel that clicks steps a column per notch.

enabled.description: true scrolls strips with the mouse.

modifier.description: The modifiers held, exactly these, joined by -. Not [drag] mouse-modifier while drag is on, nor the modifier of a switcher whose trigger is hold; a double-tap switcher's can be shared.

drag.description: Whether a press dragged across with the modifier scrolls the strip.

wheel.description: Whether a stroke with scroll phases (a Magic Mouse or trackpad swipe, a smooth wheel whose driver sends them) with the modifier scrolls the strip, and any other wheel steps a column per notch, at most every 120 ms.

cursor.description: Whether the pointer shows an open hand over a window a press with the modifier would drag, and a closed one while it drags. Ignored without drag.

speed.description: How far the strip goes for each point the pointer or the stroke moves; 1 follows the pointer.

show-switcher.description: Whether the window switcher shows the strip once it rests. Unset, [gestures.scroll]'s.

switcher-ms.description: Milliseconds the window switcher shows the strip. Unset, [gestures.scroll]'s.

edge-flash.description: Whether the display glows along the side the mouse pushes the strip past. Unset, [gestures.scroll]'s.

modifiers.description: Which key of each modifier pair bindings answer to. The other key types as usual.

alt.description: Which Option key is alt in bindings.

ctrl.description: Which Control key is ctrl in bindings.

cmd.description: Which Command key is cmd in bindings.

shift.description: Which Shift key is shift in bindings.

hyper.description: The modifiers, two or more joined by -, that a switcher's modifier = 'hyper' holds together, from either side.

hooks.description: dinky commands run on events. Shell goes through exec-and-forget.

startup.description: Once, when dinky starts, after it has read the windows and displays.

workspace-changing.description: As soon as dinky starts switching a display, and again when a burst of switches changes the target. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_WORKSPACE (the target), DINKY_PREV_WORKSPACE and DINKY_DISPLAY.

workspace-changed.description: Whenever a display's current workspace changes. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_WORKSPACE, DINKY_PREV_WORKSPACE and DINKY_DISPLAY.

focus-changed.description: When the focused window changes, debounced by 50 ms.

mode-changed.description: When the binding mode changes, including back to main when the config reloads. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_MODE and DINKY_PREV_MODE.

display-changed.description: When a display connects or disconnects. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_DISPLAYS and DINKY_PREV_DISPLAYS, how many displays there are now and were before.

rules.description: Rules for new windows. Every rule whose conditions all match runs, in order; for layout floating and layout tiling the last one wins.

app-id.description: The app's bundle ID, e.g. com.apple.Safari.

app-id-regex.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's bundle ID, e.g. ^com\.apple\. for every Apple app.

app-name.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's name.

title.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the window title.

disk-image.description: Whether the window comes from a mounted disk image: a Finder window showing a .dmg's contents, or a window of an app run from one.

workspace-layout.description: The layout of the window's workspace as the rule's commands run, or a list of them. free is a workspace that does not tile (layout = 'free' or tiling = false); floating is its old name.

workspace.description: The number of the window's workspace as the rule's commands run, or a list of them.

run.description: The command or commands to run for a matching window.

mode.description: Key bindings, grouped in modes. dinky starts in main; the `mode <name>` command switches.

additionalProperties.description: Key combinations mapped to the command or commands they run, and tables named for a layout whose keys take over on a workspace laid out that way.

^(scrolling|tiles|dwindle|accordion|fixe.description: Bindings for a workspace with this layout, over the mode's own: a key here replaces the mode's, the rest stay. tiles and dwindle are one layout.

hapticStrength.description: light, medium (as macOS's own taps) or strong.

gaps.description: Gaps in points. A side or axis left out keeps its default.

inner.description: Points between tiled windows: one value for both axes, or per axis.

outer.description: Points between tiled windows and the screen edge: one value, or per side.

highlight.description: A highlight colour, '#rrggbb' or '#rrggbbaa', or accent for the accent colour in System Settings.

command.description: A dinky command, as `dinky help` lists them: `workspace 3`, `layout floating`, `exec-and-forget open -a Safari`.

commands.description: A command or a list of commands, run in order.

hook.description: A command or a list of commands, run in order. May be empty.

keyCombo.description: Zero or more modifiers (alt, ctrl, cmd, shift, or the shorthands hyper and meh) and one key name, joined by '-': alt-shift-h, ctrl-left, alt-page-up, hyper-1, f5.
